title: Usage of ContextVar's in FastAPI
question_body: ### First Check - [X] I added a very descriptive title here. - [X] I used the GitHub search to find a similar question and didn't find it. - [X] I searched the FastAPI documentation, with the integrated search. - [X] I already searched in Google "How to X in FastAPI" and didn't find any information. - [X] I already read and followed all the tutorial in the docs and didn't find an answer. - [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [Pydantic](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic). - [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [Swagger UI](https://github.com/swagger-api/swagger-ui). - [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [ReDoc](https://github.com/Redocly/redoc). ### Commit to Help - [X] I commit to help with one of those options 👆 ### Example Code ```python https://github.com/claeyswo/fastapi_poc/tree/main ``` ### Description Hello, We're in the process of migrating our entire codebase from Pyramid to FastAPI. Due to some legacy architectural choices we ended up with a lot of endpoints that accept and return slightly different content based on a users roles, sometimes in combination with the state of the db model. This is something we're going to address in the future, but for the time being, I came up with an idea that uses Pydantic discriminators to dynamically determine the request and response schemas. I have a little testapp [here](https://github.com/claeyswo/fastapi_poc/tree/main). The relevant sections are: - [Route that defines the create endpoint](https://github.com/claeyswo/fastapi_poc/blob/6edd3b189173786a72a276a4ca09804470ae805e/app/routers/premies.py#L26) - [Discriminated unions](https://github.com/claeyswo/fastapi_poc/blob/6edd3b189173786a72a276a4ca09804470ae805e/app/schemas.py#L289) - [And finally the discriminator itself](https://github.com/claeyswo/fastapi_poc/blob/6edd3b189173786a72a276a4ca09804470ae805e/app/schemas.py#L17) Which also renders nicely in the docs. Now the thing is that I use ContextVar's to inject userinfo into my discriminator. And I found [this](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/release-notes/?h=contextvar#features_41). `Note: You probably don't need contextvars, and you should probably avoid using them. ` I know there are libraries that make extensive use of them, like starlette-context, but I don't know if I can use that as a reference. And my other team members all have their doubts about using them. So my question is: Should this be avoided? Is it ok? Are there any pitfalls? ### Operating System Linux ### Operating System Details _No response_ ### FastAPI Version 0.128.7 ### Pydantic Version 2.12.5 ### Python Version Python 3.11.11 ### Additional Context _No response_
accepted_answer:
Context vars can be difficult to deal with, they can be complex and hard to debug, depending on how you use them. But given you already have some complex code, they are probably right for your use case.

Here are the caveats:

In FastAPI, you need to set them in an `async` dependency function or path operation, or an async middleware. If the function is non-async, FastAPI will run it on a thread worker. And if the context var is set on a thread worker, that is, let's say, a "child" context, so the value will **not** be propagated upwards.

So, you need to set the context in an async function.

Now, if the code that gets the data to be set is non-async blocking code (e.g. calling a DB), and if you run it directly on the async function, it will block the event loop, blocking any other operation.

So, you will likely need to set the context var in an async function to some container (e.g. a dict) and then in the non-async blocking function that gets the data and sets the actual value (e.g. a user object), you can get the container value from the context var, and set the user inside of that container. This way, the blocking function is never really setting the value in the context var, it's only accessing it (the container), and modifying that container.

So, you will probably need something like this:

```Python
from contextvars import ContextVar
from typing import Annotated

from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI

app = FastAPI()

# The context var holds a container (dict), not the final value directly
request_context: ContextVar[dict] = ContextVar("request_context")


async def set_context():
    """Async dependency that initializes the context var with a container.

    Must be async so the context var is set in the main async task,
    not in a thread worker.
    """
    ctx: dict = {}
    token = request_context.set(ctx)
    yield ctx
    request_context.reset(token)


def get_user_from_db(ctx: Annotated[dict, Depends(set_context)]) -> dict:
    """Sync dependency, runs in a thread worker.

    It receives the container from set_context and mutates it.
    It never calls request_context.set(), only reads and mutates the
    existing container, so the child-context limitation doesn't apply.
    """
    # Simulate blocking DB lookup
    user = {"id": 1, "name": "Alice", "role": "admin"}
    ctx["user"] = user
    return user


@app.get("/")
async def root(user: Annotated[dict, Depends(get_user_from_db)]):
    return {
        "user": user,
        "role_from_ctx": request_context.get().get("user", {}).get("role"),
    }
```

### Example Code

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI, Query, Depends
from typing import Annotated
from pydantic import BaseModel

app = FastAPI()

class Old(BaseModel):
    old_username: str = "old"
    old_phone: str | None = None

class New(BaseModel):
    new_username: str = "new"
    new_phone: str | None = None

@app.get("/params_query")
async def params_query(
    query_new: Annotated[New, Query()],
    query_single: Annotated[int | None, Query()] = None,
    query_old: Old = Depends(),
):
    return {
        "query_new": query_new,
        "query_single": query_single,
        "query_old": query_old,
    }
```


### Description

When using Annotated[Model, Query()] as a query parameter, FastAPI fails to recognize it if there is also a single query parameter (e.g., int | None) in the same handler. However, using Depends() instead of Annotated[Model, Query()] works fine.And using both two schema style query parameter,it also works fine.

### Operating System

Windows

### Operating System Details

_No response_

### FastAPI Version

0.115.11

### Pydantic Version

2.10.6

### Python Version

3.11.9

### Additional Context

_No response_
accepted_answer: This is a known limitation. For now combining Query model with single parameters or combining several Query models in one path operation is not supported

title: Giving string to Security `scopes` creates each character as a different scope
question_body:

- [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [ReDoc](https://github.com/Redocly/redoc).

### Commit to Help

- [X] I commit to help with one of those options 👆

### Example Code

```python
"""Test code for oauth scopes in Security dependencies, can be executed with pytest"""

from typing import Annotated
from fastapi import FastAPI, Security
from fastapi.params import Depends
from fastapi.security import OAuth2PasswordBearer
from fastapi.security.oauth2 import SecurityScopes
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

app = FastAPI()

oauth2_scheme = OAuth2PasswordBearer(
    tokenUrl="token",
    scopes={"me": "Read information about the current user.", "items": "Read items."},
)


def get_security_scopes(
    security_scopes: SecurityScopes, token: Annotated[str, Depends(oauth2_scheme)]
):
    return security_scopes.scopes


@app.get("/me")
async def read_single_scope(
    current_scope: Annotated[list[str], Security(get_security_scopes, scopes="me")],
):
    return {"scopes": current_scope}


@app.get("/me-and-items")
async def read_single_scope(
    current_scope: Annotated[
        list[str], Security(get_security_scopes, scopes=["me", "items"])
    ],
):
    return {"scopes": current_scope}


client = TestClient(app)


def test_single_scope_string():
    response = client.get("/me", headers={"Authorization": "Bearer sometoken"})

    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert response.json() == {"scopes": ["me"]}


def test_list_scopes():
    response = client.get(
        "/me-and-items", headers={"Authorization": "Bearer sometoken"}
    )

    assert response.status_code == 200
```


### Description

Hi, i found an unexpected behavior when declaring scopes for a security dependencies.
When defining the scopes parameter, we can currently give a single string, because a string is also a sequence of strings
https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/blob/eea196f4a505c2584fafda691f2a0033c4db6622/fastapi/params.py#L782.
But then all characters of the string become different scopes

In the test file for the example code, currently. The `read_single_scope` route will return:

```python
{"scopes":["m","e"]}
```

Instead of the most logical:
```python
{"scopes":["me"]}
```


It can be corrected by this simple modification on `Security`'s constructor:

Changing this line:
https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/blob/eea196f4a505c2584fafda691f2a0033c4db6622/fastapi/params.py#L786

To this:
```python
if isinstance(scopes, str):
            self.scopes = [scopes]
        else:
            self.scopes = scopes or []
```

### Operating System

Linux

### Operating System Details

Debian 12

### FastAPI Version

0.115.8

### Pydantic Version

2.10.6

### Python Version

Python 3.13.1

### Additional Context

_No response_
accepted_answer:
@YuriiMotov strings are indeed a sequence of strings, but currently this allows to pass a single string instead of any other sequence of strings elements to the `scopes` parameter and this can be misleading to new developers, as they would only find out the error during runtime.

I proposed a fix in #13369 to create a list with the single string when passing a string to `scopes`, it maintains the existing typing and handles this edge case.

question_body:

- [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [Swagger UI](https://github.com/swagger-api/swagger-ui).
- [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [ReDoc](https://github.com/Redocly/redoc).

### Commit to Help

- [X] I commit to help with one of those options 👆

### Example Code

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI, Query
from pydantic import BaseModel


class C(BaseModel):
    cname: str

class B(BaseModel):
    bname: str
    child: C

class A(BaseModel):
    aname: str
    child: B

app = FastAPI()

@app.get("/")
def route(a: A = Query()):
    return a

if __name__ == "__main__":
    import uvicorn
    uvicorn.run(app, host="localhost", port=7777)
```


### Description

* Open browser
* Call `/` endpoint and fill out `aname` with something random
* It makes the following request `http://localhost:7777/?aname=asdf&bname=string&child=%7B%22cname%22%3A%22string%22%7D`
* You receive the following error

```json
{
  "detail": [
    {
      "type": "model_attributes_type",
      "loc": [
        "query",
        "child"
      ],
      "msg": "Input should be a valid dictionary or object to extract fields from",
      "input": "{\"cname\":\"string\"}"
    }
  ]
}
```

* It's unclear how to use nested models in query parameter or if they're supported in fastapi.

### Operating System

Windows

### Operating System Details

_No response_

### FastAPI Version

0.116.1

### Pydantic Version

2.11.7

### Python Version

Python 3.12.9

### Additional Context

_No response_
accepted_answer:
FastAPI doesn't support nested models for query parameters.
Supporting [DeepObject serialization](https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/issues/3163) would be helpful here.

For now, use `Body` parameters (as @valentinDruzhinin suggested) or consider using the following idea:

Change type of `A.child` to `Json[B]` and override its schema using `WithJsonSchema`
```py
class A(BaseModel):
    aname: str
    child: Annotated[Json[B], WithJsonSchema({"type": "string"})]
```

Runnable code example:

```py
from typing import Annotated

from fastapi import FastAPI, Query
from pydantic import BaseModel, Json, TypeAdapter, WithJsonSchema

class C(BaseModel):
    cname: str

class B(BaseModel):
    bname: str
    child: C

class A(BaseModel):
    aname: str
    child: Annotated[Json[B], WithJsonSchema({"type": "string"})]

app = FastAPI()
AAdapter = TypeAdapter(A)

@app.get("/")
def route(a: A = Query()):
    return a
```
Send request as `http://localhost:8000/?aname=a&child=%7B%22bname%22%3A%20%22b%22%2C%20%22child%22%3A%20%7B%22cname%22%3A%20%22c%22%7D%7D`.
Here the part after `child=` is url-encoded value of `{"bname": "b", "child": {"cname": "c"}}`.
This way you will have request validation working for nested models

question_body:

- [X] I already read and followed all the tutorial in the docs and didn't find an answer.
- [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [Pydantic](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic).
- [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [Swagger UI](https://github.com/swagger-api/swagger-ui).
- [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [ReDoc](https://github.com/Redocly/redoc).

### Commit to Help

- [X] I commit to help with one of those options 👆

### Example Code

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
from fastapi.responses import StreamingResponse
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
import asyncio, json, time

@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
    print("startup")
    yield
    print("shutdown")  # <-- this is never called if SSE is connected

app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)

@app.get("/sse/{uuid}")
async def sse(uuid: str, request: Request):
    async def generate():
        try:
            while not request.is_disconnected():
                yield f"data: {json.dumps({'uuid': uuid, 'ts': time.time()})}\n\n"
                await asyncio.sleep(1)
        except asyncio.CancelledError:
            print(f"SSE {uuid} cancelled")
            raise
        finally:
            print(f"SSE {uuid} closed")

    return StreamingResponse(generate(), media_type="text/event-stream")
```


### Description

Hi, I’m using FastAPI with a StreamingResponse endpoint for Server-Sent Events (SSE).
Everything works fine while the client is connected.

But when I press Ctrl+C to stop the server, if there’s still an active SSE connection, the application does not trigger the lifespan shutdown.

### Operating System

Linux

### Operating System Details

_No response_

### FastAPI Version

0.116.1

### Pydantic Version

2.11.7

### Python Version

3.13.5

### Additional Context

_No response_
accepted_answer:
Assuming that you are using uvicorn - I believe this is the expected graceful shutdown behavior. Graceful shutdown means to stop the server only when it is safe to do so, i.e., when all active connections are closed. Say, you are downloading a 1MB file via plain HTTP protocol at the speed of 1KB/s from the server. Uvicorn will have to wait for 1000 seconds before it can quit gracefully.

If you really can't change your application logic to avoid long connections, consider passing the `timeout_graceful_shutdown` argument to uvicorn to set a hard limit. Note that this will break the gracefulness and may cause some connections to be interrupted.

### Commit to Help

- [X] I commit to help with one of those options 👆

### Example Code

```python
from typing import Annotated, Callable
from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI, Header

app = FastAPI()

def get_user_browser(user_agent: str = Header(default="")):
    browser = user_agent.split(' ')[0]
    return browser

def get_greeting_message(browser: Annotated[str, Depends(get_user_browser)]):
    return f"Hello, {browser} user!"

class GreetingGenerator:    
    def __init__(self, greeting_provider: Callable[..., str]):
        self.greeting_provider = greeting_provider
    
    def __call__(self):
        message = self.greeting_provider()
        return {"message": message}

greeter = GreetingGenerator(greeting_provider=Depends(get_greeting_message))

@app.get("/hello")
async def hello(
    greeting: Annotated[dict, Depends(greeter)]
):
    return greeting
```


### Description

How to pass a "callback" callable that itself uses dependencies to a dependency?

Using the approach above, it throws a `TypeError: 'Depends' object is not callable`.

Linux

_No response_

### FastAPI Version

0.115.12

### Pydantic Version

2.11.3

### Python Version

3.12.9

### Additional Context

I want to use this feature to make a fine-grained cache system based on dependencies. It requires access to the database context and to [`BackgroundTasks`](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/background-tasks/).

title: [ FastAPI Docs ] Should the `Previous Steps before Starting` include `LifeSpan`?
question_body:
I was just reading through the documentation - [here](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/deployment/concepts/#previous-steps-before-starting)

I see that in the section `Previous Steps before Starting` have mentioned about database migration, staring other process before starting the API, will it be logical to introduce `LIfeSpan` here?

Life span docs - [here](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/advanced/events/#lifespan)

Sample code:
```python
@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
    # Load the ML model
    ml_models["answer_to_everything"] = fake_answer_to_everything_ml_model
    yield
    # Clean up the ML models and release the resources
    ml_models.clear()
```
accepted_answer:
This section is about operations you want to perform **once** before you start the app.
`lifespan` is executed **once per worker**. So, it's not suitable here..

> But in most cases, you will want to perform these steps only once.
> 
> So, you will want to have a single process to perform those previous steps, before starting the application.

title: Bug with complex fields (`list[str]`) inside `BaseModel`
question_body:
### Privileged issue

- [x] I'm @tiangolo or he asked me directly to create an issue here.

### Issue Content

## Summary
When "complex" (e.g., `list[str]`) field is definied inside `BaseModel`, it doesn't get parsed.

## MRE1
### Summary
Example when "complex" field defined in `BaseModel` doesn't get parsed.

#### Code
```python
from typing import Annotated
import uvicorn
from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI, Query
from pydantic import BaseModel

class MyParams(BaseModel):
    size: Annotated[int | None, Query()] = None
    field: Annotated[list[str] | None, Query()] = None

app = FastAPI()

@app.get("/items")
async def get_items(
    params: Annotated[MyParams, Depends()],
) -> None:
    print("params: ", params)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    uvicorn.run(app, host="127.0.0.1", port=8000)
```

#### Request:
```bash
curl --location 'localhost:8000/items?size=100&field=foo&field=bar'
```

#### Expected:
```text
params:  size=100 field=foo,bar
INFO:     127.0.0.1:54972 - "GET /items?size=100&field=foo&field=bar HTTP/1.1" 200 OK
```

#### Actual:
```text
params:  size=100 field=None
INFO:     127.0.0.1:54972 - "GET /items?size=100&field=foo&field=bar HTTP/1.1" 200 OK
```

## MRE2
### Summary
Example when "complex" field is moved from `BaseModel` to a separate attribute and gets parsed.

#### Code
```python
from typing import Annotated
import uvicorn
from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI, Query
from pydantic import BaseModel

class MyParams(BaseModel):
    size: Annotated[int | None, Query()] = None

app = FastAPI()

@app.get("/items")
async def get_items(
    params: Annotated[MyParams, Depends()],
    field: Annotated[list[str] | None, Query()] = None,
) -> None:
    print("params: ", params)
    print("field: ", field)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    uvicorn.run(app, host="127.0.0.1", port=8000)
```

#### Request:
```bash
curl --location 'localhost:8000/items?size=100&field=foo&field=bar'
```

#### Expected:
```text
params:  size=100
field:  ['foo', 'bar']
INFO:     127.0.0.1:55020 - "GET /items?size=100&field=foo&field=bar HTTP/1.1" 200 OK
```

#### Actual:
```text
params:  size=100
field:  ['foo', 'bar']
INFO:     127.0.0.1:55020 - "GET /items?size=100&field=foo&field=bar HTTP/1.1" 200 OK
```

### Versions
```text

def get_my_obj(
    session: SessionDep,
    objectid: int = fastapi.Path(..., example = 5)
) -> list[MY_OBJ]:
```


### Description

I've added the following code to my app:

```
@app.get("/v0/my_obj/{objectid}")
def get_my_obj(
    session: SessionDep,
    objectid: int = fastapi.Path(..., example = 5)
) -> list[MY_OBJ]:
```

The app generates the following warning during startup:

DeprecationWarning: `example` has been deprecated, please use `examples` instead

The new examples config is useful when describing the full shape of an object. However, my API returns a list of objects, and there is no way to define default params on a list without using the fastapi.Path hint shown above.

accepted_answer: `example` property is deprecated by openapi specification. FastAPI just follows the specification. See: https://spec.openapis.org/oas/v3.1.0#fixed-fields-19 --- Use `examples` and `openapi_examples`: ```py from typing import Annotated from fastapi import FastAPI, Path from pydantic import BaseModel, Field class MY_OBJ(BaseModel): id: Annotated[int, Field(examples=[5])] name: Annotated[int, Field(examples=["object name example"])] app = FastAPI() @app.get("/v0/my_obj/{objectid}") def get_my_obj( objectid: int = Path(..., openapi_examples={"example1": {"value": 5}}), ) -> list[MY_OBJ]: pass ```

question_body:
### First Check

- [X] I added a very descriptive title here.
- [X] I used the GitHub search to find a similar question and didn't find it.
- [X] I searched the FastAPI documentation, with the integrated search.
- [X] I already searched in Google "How to X in FastAPI" and didn't find any information.
- [X] I already read and followed all the tutorial in the docs and didn't find an answer.
- [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [Pydantic](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic).
- [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [Swagger UI](https://github.com/swagger-api/swagger-ui).
- [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [ReDoc](https://github.com/Redocly/redoc).

### Commit to Help

- [X] I commit to help with one of those options 👆

### Example Code

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI

app = FastAPI()

users_router = APIRouter(prefix="/users", tags=["users"])


@users_router.get("/{user_id}")
def read_user(user_id: str):
    return {"user_id": user_id}


items_router = APIRouter(prefix="/{user_id}/items", tags=["items"])


@items_router.get("/{id}")
def read_item(user_id: str, id: str):
    return {"user_id": user_id, "id": id}


users_router.include_router(items_router)

app.include_router(users_router)
```


### Description

In this example, I'm using nested routers by calling `include_router` on a parent router. It's convenient to avoid repetition of the prefix of the parent one.

Is there a way to avoid duplication of the `Read Item` endpoint in the docs (ie. Swagger UI)? This endpoint appears twice, in both the `users` and `items` section.

I know it's possible to avoid the repetition by providing the `tags` to individual endpoints instead of doing it at the router level but it will be a bit tedious when adding more endpoints.

### Operating System

Linux

### Operating System Details

_No response_

### FastAPI Version

0.136.3

### Pydantic Version

2.13.4

### Python Version

Python 3.10.20

### Additional Context

_No response_
accepted_answer:
This is expected from how FastAPI combines router metadata. Tags from the parent router and the child router both end up on the nested operation, and Swagger UI shows an operation under every tag it has. So your item route is not duplicated as a route, it is displayed in both tag groups.

There is not a clean switch that means "inherit the parent prefix but not the parent tags" for only the nested router. The usual workaround is to split the prefix-only grouping router from the tagged routers:

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI

app = FastAPI()

# Prefix-only router. No tags here.
users_prefix = APIRouter(prefix="/users")

users_router = APIRouter(tags=["users"])

@users_router.get("/{user_id}")
def read_user(user_id: str):
    return {"user_id": user_id}

items_router = APIRouter(prefix="/{user_id}/items", tags=["items"])

@items_router.get("/{id}")
def read_item(user_id: str, id: str):
    return {"user_id": user_id, "id": id}

users_prefix.include_router(users_router)
users_prefix.include_router(items_router)

app.include_router(users_prefix)
```

That keeps the URL nesting but prevents the `items` endpoints from inheriting the `users` tag. If most routes under `/users` should be tagged `users`, then tagging individual direct user endpoints is the more explicit option.

If this solves it, please mark this comment as the answer so other people can find it faster.

from fastapi import FastAPI

app = FastAPI()

@app.exception_handler(Exception)
async def general_exception_handler(request: Request, exception: Exception):
    await ErrorLogger.log_error(exception=exception, request=request)
    raise HTTPException(
        status_code=500, detail=f"Internal server error: {str(exception)}"
    )
```


### Description

I am trying to create a general exception handler that will perform specific logging when an exception occurs and then raise a HTTP exception. I'm trying to log the body as well, but when I do that I get an error: "Receive channel has not been made available". I've been able to find some other issues on the topic (i.e. https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/issues/1216 and https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/issues/3677), but they were quite old and used an old version of FastAPI. 

Is there currently a way to receive the body in an exception handler to log it?

### Operating System

Windows

### Operating System Details

_No response_

### FastAPI Version

0.116.1

### Pydantic Version

2.11.7

### Python Version

3.11.9

_No response_
accepted_answer:
~You're hitting a known limitation in FastAPI/Starlette: by the time the exception handler runs, the request body has likely already been consumed (and can't be read again).~ You need to read and store the request body in middleware, before any endpoint or error handler consumes it.

Working code example:
```
from fastapi import FastAPI, Request, HTTPException
from starlette.middleware.base import BaseHTTPMiddleware
from starlette.responses import JSONResponse

app = FastAPI()

# Middleware to capture the request body
class BodyCaptureMiddleware(BaseHTTPMiddleware):
    async def dispatch(self, request: Request, call_next):
        request.state.body = await request.body()
        response = await call_next(request)
        return response

app.add_middleware(BodyCaptureMiddleware)

# Fake logger
class ErrorLogger:
    @staticmethod
    async def log_error(exception: Exception, request: Request):
        body = getattr(request.state, "body", b"[unavailable]")
        print("Logging error:", exception)
        print("Request body:", body.decode("utf-8", errors="ignore"))

# General exception handler
@app.exception_handler(Exception)
async def general_exception_handler(request: Request, exception: Exception):
    await ErrorLogger.log_error(exception=exception, request=request)
    return JSONResponse(
        status_code=500,
        content={"detail": f"Internal server error: {str(exception)}"},
    )

@app.post("/crash")
async def crash_endpoint(payload: dict):
    # Simulate error
    raise ValueError("Simulated error for testing!")

```
Results:
```
INFO:     127.0.0.1:65431 - "GET /openapi.json HTTP/1.1" 200 OK
Logging error: Simulated error for testing!
Request body: {
  "additionalProp1": {}
}
INFO:     127.0.0.1:65437 - "POST /crash HTTP/1.1" 500 Internal Server Error
```

Description: I am using FastAPI with routers and access tokens to fetch user data. When I send a request using Postman, the request is successful, and the expected response is returned. However, when I try the same request using Swagger (FastAPI's auto-generated docs), I receive a "Not Found" error.

Steps to Reproduce:

Define a route that requires an access token, as shown in the provided code snippet.
Send a request to the route using Postman with the correct access token.
Observe that the request is successful.
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b85129c8-843d-4ddb-aac9-ea99bc35c787)

Send the same request using Swagger with the same access token.
Observe that Swagger returns a "undefined" error.

Hello @m8811163008,

swagger is expecting to received this response format from `login_for_access_token`

```
I'm quite sure you are not returning that format and swagger will read 'access_token' as undefined.

- [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [Swagger UI](https://github.com/swagger-api/swagger-ui).
- [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [ReDoc](https://github.com/Redocly/redoc).

### Commit to Help

- [X] I commit to help with one of those options 👆

### Example Code

```python
from typing import Annotated
import time
import threading

from fastapi import FastAPI,Depends

app = FastAPI()
class GlobalCounter:
    def __init__(self):
        self._count = 0

    def increment(self):
        current = self._count
        time.sleep(0.001)  # artificial delay
        self._count = current + 1

    def get_count(self):
        return self._count

counter = GlobalCounter()
lock = threading.Lock()
def get_counter():
    with lock:
        yield counter

@app.get("/increment")
def increment_dep(c: Annotated[int,Depends(get_counter)]) -> None:
    c.increment()
    print(counter.get_count())


# and run  apache bench
# ab -n 2000 -c 100 http://127.0.0.1:8000/increment_dep
```


### Description

Deadlock when the concurrency is above 40, and ONLY when the get_counter is a Depends.

If you manually create and use a context manager, it does not lock up.

```
@contextlib.contextmanager
def get_counter2():
    with lock:
        yield counter
        
 @app.get("/increment_dep2")
def increment_dep2() -> None:
    with get_counter2() as c:
        c.increment()
    print(counter.get_count())
```

```
ab -n 2000 -c 100 http://127.0.0.1:8000/increment_dep2
```

### Operating System

Linux

### Operating System Details

_No response_

### FastAPI Version

0.115.8

### Pydantic Version

2.10.6

### Python Version

Python 3.13.1

### Additional Context

_No response_
accepted_answer:
Hello @y2kbugger i'll try to explain what is wrong in your code and what is happening.

The problem with your code is that the deadlock happens due to thread exhaustion.

Basically the depency `c: Annotated[GlobalCounter, Depends(get_counter)` is the one that is exhausting the threadpool due the lock and since your endpoint function is sync ( so need a thread ), at some point you will not have any available thread to execute it and since you cannot execute it your dependency will never be released and with that the lock.

A short simple example: suppose to limit the pool to 2 threads and the are 3 incoming requests.

r1 -> solve dependency and lock
r2 -> trying solve dependecy and is wait for the lock
r3 -> is waiting for a thread

r1 with the dependecy solved, now try to call the endpoint function but is sync so need a thread where can be executed but there are no thread available. Here all is blocked forever.

In your second example where you have all inside the endpoint all works because only the endpoint thread is required and you are already inside it.

To fix the first example, just trasform 

`def increment_dep(c: Annotated[GlobalCounter, Depends(get_counter)]) -> None:`
in 
`async def increment_dep(c: Annotated[GlobalCounter, Depends(get_counter)]) -> None:`


In general i would suggest to avoid locks inside the dependency, because you are basically serializing the requests and bringing complexity with it.

### Commit to Help

- [X] I commit to help with one of those options 👆

### Example Code

```python
"""
Demonstrates the issue with BeforeValidator in FastAPI query parameters.

When using Annotated[..., BeforeValidator(function)] as a custom type conversion
in query parameters, the BeforeValidator function is NOT called.

However, the same pattern works correctly in Pydantic models.
"""

from typing import Annotated

from fastapi import FastAPI, Query
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from pydantic import BaseModel, BeforeValidator

app = FastAPI()


def parse_comma_separated(value: str | None) -> list[str] | None:
    """Convert comma-separated string to list."""
    print(f"BeforeValidator called with: {value!r}")  # Debug: see if this gets called
    if isinstance(value, str):
        return [item.strip() for item in value.split(",") if item.strip()]
    return value


# Custom type using BeforeValidator
CommaSeparatedList = Annotated[
    list[str] | None,
    BeforeValidator(parse_comma_separated),
    Query(description="Comma-separated list of items"),
]


# This works - BeforeValidator IS called in Pydantic models
class RequestBody(BaseModel):
    items: CommaSeparatedList


@app.post("/body")
def with_body(body: RequestBody):
    """POST endpoint with body - BeforeValidator WORKS here."""
    return {"items": body.items}


@app.get("/items-none")
def items_none(items: CommaSeparatedList | None = None):
    """GET endpoint with query param - BeforeValidator does NOT work here.

    Expected: items="a,b,c" should be parsed to ["a", "b", "c"]
    Actual:
        v0.118.1: items = ["a", "b", "c"] (works)
        v0.118.2: items = None (before validator is not called)
        v0.128.0: items = None (before validator is not called)
    """
    return {"items": items}


@app.get("/items-no-validator")
def items_no_validator(items: CommaSeparatedList = None):
    """GET endpoint with query param - BeforeValidator does NOT work here.

    Expected: items="a,b,c" should be parsed to ["a", "b", "c"]
    Actual:
        v0.118.1: items = ["a,b,c"] (before validator called with ['a,b,c'])
        v0.118.2: items = ["a,b,c"] (before validator called with ['a,b,c'])
        v0.128.0: items = ["a,b,c"] (before validator called with ['a,b,c'])

    Note:
        if we remove the Query annotation with

        `
        CommaSeparatedList = Annotated[
            list[str] | None,
            BeforeValidator(parse_comma_separated),
        ]
        ```
        then it's None

    """
    return {"items": items}


def test_body():
    """POST with body - BeforeValidator WORKS here."""
    client = TestClient(app)
    response = client.post("/body", json={"items": "a,b,c"})
    print("POST /body with items='a,b,c'")
    print("  Expected: ['a', 'b', 'c'] (3 items)")
    print(f"  Response: {response.json()}")
    print()


def test_items_none():
    """GET with query param - BeforeValidator does NOT work here."""
    client = TestClient(app)
    response = client.get("/items-none", params={"items": "a,b,c"})
    print("GET /items-none?items=a,b,c")
    print("  Expected: ['a', 'b', 'c'] (3 items)")
    print(f"  Response: {response.json()}")
    print()


def test_items_no_validator():
    """GET with query param - BeforeValidator does NOT work here with 0.118.1 and 0.118.2."""
    client = TestClient(app)
    response = client.get("/items-no-validator", params={"items": "a,b,c"})
    print("GET /items-no-validator?items=a,b,c")
    print("  Expected: ['a', 'b', 'c'] (3 items)")
    print(f"  Response: {response.json()}")
    print()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print("Testing BeforeValidator with FastAPI\n")
    test_body()
    test_items_none()
    test_items_no_validator()
```


### Description

# FastAPI BeforeValidator issue

We use Annotated + BeforeValidator to automatically convert query parameters like "items=a,b,c" into lists.

Starting in v0.118.2, the annotation doesn't work as expected anymore.

## Description

When using Annotated[..., BeforeValidator(function)] as a custom type conversion in query parameters, the function is not called.


## Versions

- 0.118.1 works ok
- 0.118.2 has the issue.

Probably introduced in https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/pull/12942

## Relevant links

Related: https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/issues/13440
Docs: https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/query-params-str-validations/#custom-validation

### Operating System

macOS

### Operating System Details

_No response_

### FastAPI Version

0.128.0

### Pydantic Version

2.11.9

### Python Version

 3.13.11

### Additional Context

annotated-doc==0.0.4
annotated-types==0.7.0
anyio==4.12.1
certifi==2026.1.4
click==8.3.1
fastapi==0.128.0
h11==0.16.0
httpcore==1.0.9
httpx==0.27.2
idna==3.11
pydantic==2.11.9
pydantic_core==2.33.2
sniffio==1.3.1
starlette==0.48.0
typing-inspection==0.4.2
typing_extensions==4.15.0
uvicorn==0.40.0
accepted_answer:
Before 0.118.2 there was a bug and FastAPI failed to correctly recognize the list type if it was specified using `Annotated` inside the `Union` (like `Annotated[list[str], Query()] | None`).

In 0.118.2 that bug was fixed and FastAPI now parses this parameter as list and passes list with one element to validator. You can see this in printed log: `BeforeValidator called with: ['a,b,c']`.

So, to fix your code example you need to modify `parse_comma_separated` to handle `value` parameter passes as list:

```
def parse_comma_separated(value: str | list | None) -> list[str] | None:
    """Convert comma-separated string to list."""
    print(f"BeforeValidator called with: {value!r}")  # Debug: see if this gets called
    if isinstance(value, list) and len(value) == 1:
        value = value[0]
    if isinstance(value, str):
        return [item.strip() for item in value.split(",") if item.strip()]
    return value
```

And, you don't need to use union in `items: CommaSeparatedList | None = None` - just `items: CommaSeparatedList = None` is correct since `CommaSeparatedList` is already `list[str] | None`

### Commit to Help

- [x] I commit to help with one of those options 👆

### Example Code

```python
user_oauth2_scheme = OAuth2PasswordBearer(tokenUrl='/api/auth/token', scheme_name="oauth2_scheme")
admin_oauth2_scheme = OAuth2PasswordBearer(tokenUrl='/api/auth/admin/token', scheme_name="admin_oauth2_scheme")


def get_user_from_scheme(schema:Optional[Role]=Role.user, with_sub:bool=False):
    if schema == Role.user:
        scheme = oauth2_scheme
    else:
        scheme = admin_oauth2_scheme
    async def get_current_user(token:Annotated[str, Depends(scheme)], db:AsyncSession=Depends(get_db), flow:UserAuthenticateFlow=Depends(get_user_auth_flow)):
        user = await flow(db=db, token=token, with_sub=with_sub)
        return user
    return get_current_user


def min_tier(min_tier:Tier):
    async def checker(user:User = Depends()): #### <- Root of the question is here.
        if TIER_LEVEL[user.tier] <= TIER_LEVEL[min_tier]:
            raise HTTPException(
                status_code=status.HTTP_403_FORBIDDEN,
                detail=f"Insufficient tier. Required at least {min_tier}"
            )
        return user
    return checker


@router.get('/extract_map')
async def extract_map(user:User=Depends(min_tier(Tier.Mid))):
    return {'message' : 'Hey im premium feature'}
```


### Description

### is there any way to automatically get user token from multiple oauth2 schema?

Based on my code, the min_tier factory dependency injection function receives the minimum tier to access a protected routes. The key thing of this is i want this tier checking function ignore the tier checking if user's role is admin or higher, but since the token location were different between user and admin, i've no idea about this.

### Operating System

macOS

### Operating System Details

_No response_

### FastAPI Version

0.115.14

### Pydantic Version

2.9.2

### Python Version

3.12.4

### Additional Context

i've tried putting request:Request inside the min_tier factory as a param, indeed the request is detected however it's a new blank request which doesnt contain the token.

### Current approach
So after scratching my head for a day. My approach looks like this below.

```python
async def get_token_from_any_scheme(request:Request):
    schemas = [oauth2_scheme, admin_oauth2_scheme]
    for schema in schemas:
        try:
            token = await schema(request)
            return token ### if token was found, break the loop.
        except HTTPException:
            continue
    raise HTTPException(
        status_code=status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED,
        detail='Not authenticated.',
        headers={'WWW-Authenticate' : 'Bearer'}
    )

def get_user_from_any_schema(with_sub:bool=False):
    async def get_current_user(token:str=Depends(get_token_from_any_scheme), db:AsyncSession=Depends(get_db), flow:UserAuthenticateFlow=Depends(get_user_auth_flow)):
        return await flow(db=db, token=token, with_sub=with_sub)
    return get_current_user


def min_tier(min_tier:Tier):
    async def checker(user:User = Depends(get_user_from_any_schema(with_sub=True))):
        if ROLE_LEVEL[user.role] >= ROLE_LEVEL[Role.admin]:
            return user
        if TIER_LEVEL[user.subscriptions[0].plan.tier.name] >= TIER_LEVEL[min_tier]:
            raise HTTPException(
                status_code=status.HTTP_403_FORBIDDEN,
                detail=f"Insufficient tier. Required at least {min_tier}"
            )
        return user
    return checker

@router.get('/extract_map')
async def extract_map(user:User=Depends(min_tier(min_tier=Tier.Mid))):
    return {'message' : 'Hey im premium feature'}
```
However, this approach cannot be used if you test the endpoint via swagger ui as in the endpoint there's no related connection to an instance of oauth2 password bearer object so swagger ui wont automatically attach the authorization header if you access the protected endpoint. But i think [@valentinDruzhinin] (https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/discussions/13985#discussioncomment-14084380) approach will works if you are testing the endpoint via swagger ui.
accepted_answer:
Try to treat both logins as the same `Bearer token` at request time and pick whichever token is present. Then your min_tier just depends on the unified `current user` dependency.
Try to use the example like that:
```
from typing import Annotated, Optional
from fastapi import Depends, HTTPException, Security, status
from fastapi.security import OAuth2PasswordBearer

user_oauth2 = OAuth2PasswordBearer(
    tokenUrl="/api/auth/token", scheme_name="user", auto_error=False
)
admin_oauth2 = OAuth2PasswordBearer(
    tokenUrl="/api/auth/admin/token", scheme_name="admin", auto_error=False
)

async def get_current_user(
    user_token: Annotated[Optional[str], Security(user_oauth2)],
    admin_token: Annotated[Optional[str], Security(admin_oauth2)],
    db: AsyncSession = Depends(get_db),
    flow: UserAuthenticateFlow = Depends(get_user_auth_flow),
) -> User:
    token = admin_token or user_token
    if not token:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED, detail="Not authenticated"
        )
    # Your flow should decode the token and return the User (role/tier in claims/DB)
    return await flow(db=db, token=token, with_sub=False)

def min_tier(required: Tier):
    async def checker(user: User = Depends(get_current_user)):
        # bypass if admin (adjust roles as you use them)
        if getattr(user, "role", None) in {Role.admin, Role.superadmin}:
            return user

        if TIER_LEVEL[user.tier] < TIER_LEVEL[required]:
            raise HTTPException(
                status_code=status.HTTP_403_FORBIDDEN,
                detail=f"Insufficient tier. Required at least {required}",
            )
        return user
    return checker

@router.get("/extract_map", dependencies=[Security(user_oauth2), Security(admin_oauth2)])
async def extract_map(_: User = Depends(min_tier(Tier.Mid))):
    return {"message": "Hey I'm premium feature"}
```

accepted_answer:
Great question! Here's a clear breakdown of class-based middleware in FastAPI/Starlette:

## Class-Based Middleware — Two Approaches

### 1. Pure ASGI Middleware (using `__init__` and `__call__`)
This is the lower-level approach:

from starlette.types import ASGIApp, Receive, Scope, Send

class AuthMiddleware:
    def __init__(self, app: ASGIApp):
        self.app = app

    async def __call__(self, scope: Scope, receive: Receive, send: Send):
        if scope["type"] == "http":
            # your auth logic here
            token = dict(scope.get("headers", [])).get(b"authorization", b"").decode()
            if not token:
                # reject request
                pass
        await self.app(scope, receive, send)

### 2. BaseHTTPMiddleware (using `dispatch`)
This is the higher-level, easier approach:

from starlette.middleware.base import BaseHTTPMiddleware
from starlette.requests import Request

class AuthMiddleware(BaseHTTPMiddleware):
    async def dispatch(self, request: Request, call_next):
        token = request.headers.get("authorization")
        if not token:
            return Response("Unauthorized", status_code=401)
        response = await call_next(request)
        return response

## When to use which?
- Use `dispatch` (BaseHTTPMiddleware) → simpler, cleaner, recommended for most use cases
- Use `__call__` (Pure ASGI) → better performance, needed for WebSockets or streaming

## Register in FastAPI:
app.add_middleware(AuthMiddleware)

Hope this helps! 🚀

### Example Code

```python
from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Annotated
from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI, Request

app = FastAPI()

# Function-based dependency (works fine)
def fetch_ip(request: Request) -> str:
    return request.client.host

IP = Annotated[str, Depends(fetch_ip)]

# Class-based dependency (does not work)
class IPFetcher:
    def __call__(self, request: Request) -> str:
        return request.client.host

IP = Annotated[str, Depends(IPFetcher())]  # This raises an error

@app.get("/ip")
async def ask_ip(ip: IP):
    return {"your IP address is": ip}

if __name__ == "__main__":
    from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

        response = client.get("/ip")
        response.raise_for_status()
        print(response.json())
```


### Description

When using `Depends` with a callable class and `from __future__ import annotations` enabled, FastAPI fails to resolve the dependency. However, function-based dependencies work as expected. Removing `from __future__ import annotations` resolves the issue.

# Expected behaviour
Both function-based and class-based dependencies should work consistently, regardless of `from __future__ import annotations`.

# Workaround
Removing `from __future__ import annotations` allows both implementations to work correctly.

accepted_answer:
You're right, adding class variable `__globals__ = globals()` may resolve this issue:
```python
class IPFetcher(object):
    __globals__ = globals()

    def __call__(self, request: Request) -> str:
        return request.client.host
```
This workaround works fine regradless of the line `from __future__ import annotations`.

question_body: ### First Check - [X] I added a very descriptive title here. - [X] I used the GitHub search to find a similar question and didn't find it. - [X] I searched the FastAPI documentation, with the integrated search. - [X] I already searched in Google "How to X in FastAPI" and didn't find any information. - [X] I already read and followed all the tutorial in the docs and didn't find an answer. - [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [Pydantic](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic). - [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [Swagger UI](https://github.com/swagger-api/swagger-ui). - [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [ReDoc](https://github.com/Redocly/redoc). ### Commit to Help - [X] I commit to help with one of those options 👆 ### Example Code ```python import time from fastapi import FastAPI, BackgroundTasks async def waitInLine( seconds=2, bg:BackgroundTasks=None): print(f"Stopping for {seconds} seconds") time.sleep(seconds) print(f"Done") app = FastAPI( debug=True ) @app.get('/test/bg') async def test_background_tasks( background_tasks: BackgroundTasks ): background_tasks.add_task( waitInLine, 8) return {"message": "Running a task in the background"} ``` ### Description 1. Call the URL on a browser On Windows, and running in dev mode (with `fastapi dev`), the response is sent right now, while the background task runs. With other options (`fastapi run` on the same Windows computer; and in Linux or using Docker with dev or production options), it waits for the background task to complete before sending a response I've also tried adding workers on the `fastapi run` command, but didn't work ### Operating System Windows ### Operating System Details Windows 11 (Windows NT: 10.0.22621), 64 bits ### FastAPI Version 0.115.12 ### Pydantic Version 2.11.4 ### Python Version Python 3.12.10 ### Additional Context _No response_
accepted_answer:
If you need to execute blocking code inside the `async` function, use `await run_in_threadpool()`:
```diff
async def waitInLine( seconds=2, bg:BackgroundTasks=None):
    print(f"Stopping for {seconds} seconds")
-    time.sleep(seconds)
+    await run_in_threadpool(time.sleep, seconds)
    print(f"Done")
```

Or, make you background task function sync (if you don't need to use `async` functions inside it):
```diff
- async def waitInLine( seconds=2, bg:BackgroundTasks=None):
+ def waitInLine( seconds=2, bg:BackgroundTasks=None):
    print(f"Stopping for {seconds} seconds")
    time.sleep(seconds)
    print(f"Done")
```

### Example Code

from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
import uvicorn

app = FastAPI()


def setup_post_duplicate_handler(router, subroute):
    routeName = ""
    routeEndpoint = None
    for route in router.routes:
        if route.path.endswith(subroute):
            routeName = route.name
            routeEndpoint = route.endpoint
            break

    @router.post(subroute, name=routeName)
    async def post_method(request: Request):
        print("222222")
        print(request)
        print(await request.form())
        args = await request.form()
        return await routeEndpoint(**args)


@app.middleware("http")
async def authorization(request: Request, call_next):
    print("111111")
    print(request)
    # print(await request.body())  # this command fix the problem
    print(await request.form())
    return await call_next(request)


@app.get(
    "/foo"
)
async def get_foo(name: str = '[default value]'
                  ) -> str:
    return name

setup_post_duplicate_handler(app, "/foo")

if __name__ == '__main__':
    uvicorn.run("main:app", host="127.0.0.1", port=5000, reload=False)
```


### Description

steps:
  curl -X POST http://localhost:5000/foo -d "name=123"

expected: "123"
```logs
111111
<starlette.middleware.base._CachedRequest object at 0x7f7419ef8e90>
b'name=123'
FormData([('name', '123')])
222222
<starlette.requests.Request object at 0x7f7419ef9110>
FormData([('name', '123')])
```

actual: "[default value]"
```logs
111111
<starlette.middleware.base._CachedRequest object at 0x7f66510b89d0>
FormData([('name', '123')])
222222
<starlette.requests.Request object at 0x7f66510b90d0>
FormData([])
```


requerements.txt:
```
uvicorn==0.34.2
fastapi==0.115.12

# for use multipart forms
python-multipart==0.0.20
```

### Operating System

Linux

### Operating System Details

_No response_

### FastAPI Version

0.115.12

### Pydantic Version

-

### Python Version

3.10.3

### Additional Context

if uncomment "print(await request.body())" in authorization() - the problem will gone.
if comment "print(await request.form())" in authorization() - the problem will gone.
accepted_answer:
Hello @SailorMax,

Few things to cover. This issue actually stems from Starlette’s HTTP middleware: it creates a cached copy of the request by wrapping the ASGI receive function, but it doesn’t handle some cases where the middleware itself consumes the stream (for example, via await request.form()). Once that stream is drained, downstream handlers have nothing left to read. 
Starlette discourages and may eventually stop supporting the use of this HTTP middleware, so this form-consumption case is unlikely to be fixed upstream.

> if uncomment "print(await request.body())" in authorization() - the problem will gone.

in your authorization() middleware, you force Starlette to read and cache the entire body, so later reads succeed.

> if comment "print(await request.form())" in authorization() - the problem will gone.

the middleware never drains the stream, and your endpoint can read it normally.

Also a small sidenotes:
 
``` python
await request.form()
await request.body()
```
In any case this will raise a  `RuntimeError("Stream consumed")` so i think this is not exactly a missing case but an explicit decision.

### Commit to Help

### Example Code

```python
# FastAPI Binary File Upload Corruption Issue

## Bug Summary

FastAPI is corrupting Excel (.xlsx) files during upload processing, while CSV files work perfectly. The corruption occurs before any user code processes the file, resulting in "Bad magic number for central directory" errors when attempting to open uploaded Excel files.

## Environment

- **FastAPI Version**: fastapi[standard]>=0.113.0,<0.114.0
- **Python Version**: 3.10
- **Operating System**: AWS Lambda x86_64
- **Dependencies**: 
  
  fastapi
  python-multipart
  uvicorn
  openpyxl (for testing Excel files)
  ```

## Problem Description

When uploading Excel files (.xlsx) through FastAPI's `UploadFile`, the files become corrupted during the upload processing phase, before any user application code handles them. The same endpoint works perfectly with CSV files, suggesting the issue is specific to binary file handling.

### Error Message
```
openpyxl.utils.exceptions.InvalidFileException: openpyxl does not support the old .xls file format, use xlrd to read this file, or convert it to the newer .xlsx format. Bad magic number for central directory
```

Note: The error mentions .xls but the uploaded file is .xlsx. The "Bad magic number" indicates ZIP archive corruption (XLSX files are ZIP-based).

## Code to Reproduce

### Basic Upload Endpoint

from fastapi import FastAPI, File, UploadFile, HTTPException
from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse
import os
import tempfile

app = FastAPI()

@app.post("/upload")
async def upload_file(file: UploadFile = File(...)):
    try:
        # Reset file pointer
        await file.seek(0)
        
        # Read file content
        content = await file.read()
        
        # Save to temporary file
        temp_path = f"/tmp/{file.filename}"
        with open(temp_path, "wb") as f:
            f.write(content)
        
        # Test if Excel file is readable (this is where the error occurs)
        if file.filename.lower().endswith('.xlsx'):
            import openpyxl
            wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(temp_path)  # FAILS HERE
            wb.close()
        
        os.remove(temp_path)
        return {"status": "success", "filename": file.filename}
        
    except Exception as e:
        return JSONResponse(
            status_code=400, 
            content={"error": str(e)}
        )
```

### Test Files
- **Working**: Any CSV file uploads and processes correctly
- **Failing**: Any Excel (.xlsx) file fails with "Bad magic number" error

## Attempted Solutions

All of the following approaches still result in corrupted Excel files:

### 1. File Pointer Management
```python
await file.seek(0)
content = await file.read()
```

### 2. Streaming Approach
```python
await file.seek(0)
with open(temp_path, "wb") as buffer:
    while chunk := await file.read(8192):
        buffer.write(chunk)
```

### 3. SpooledTemporaryFile
```python
with tempfile.SpooledTemporaryFile(max_size=50*1024*1024) as spooled_file:
    file_content = await file.read()
    spooled_file.write(file_content)
    # ... rest of processing
```

### 4. Raw Request Body
```python
@app.post("/upload_raw")
async def upload_raw(request: Request):
    filename = request.headers.get("X-Filename")
    body = await request.body()
    # Still corrupted when saved
```

### 5. Direct File Access
```python
underlying_file = file.file
underlying_file.seek(0)
file_data = underlying_file.read()
# Still corrupted
```

### 6. Form Data with Bytes
```python
async def upload_form_data(
    file: bytes = File(...),
    filename: str = Form(...)
):
    # Still corrupted
```

## Diagnostic Information

### File Size Comparison
- Original Excel file: X bytes
- After FastAPI processing: X bytes (same size, but corrupted content)

### Magic Number Analysis
- Valid XLSX file starts with: `PK\x03\x04` (ZIP signature)
- Corrupted file starts with: [Different bytes indicating corruption]

### Working vs Non-Working
- **CSV files**: Work perfectly with identical code
- **TXT files**: Work perfectly  
- **PDF files**: [Need to test]
- **XLSX files**: Always corrupted
- **XLS files**: [Need to test]

## Expected Behavior

Excel files should upload without corruption, maintaining their binary integrity just like CSV files do.

## Actual Behavior

Excel files are corrupted during the FastAPI upload process, becoming unreadable before any user code can process them.

## Workaround Attempts

None of the standard approaches work. Considering:
1. Switching to Flask for file uploads
2. Using external file upload service
3. Client-side preprocessing

## Additional Context

### Client-Side Upload Code
```javascript
// JavaScript fetch
const formData = new FormData();
formData.append('file', fileInput.files[0]);

fetch('/upload', {
    method: 'POST',
    body: formData
});
```

### cURL Test
```bash
curl -X POST "http://localhost:8000/upload" \
     -F "file=@test.xlsx"
```

Both methods result in the same corruption.

## Suspected Root Cause

The issue appears to be in FastAPI's underlying file processing pipeline, possibly:
1. **python-multipart**: May be corrupting binary data during multipart parsing
2. **Starlette's UploadFile**: Binary file handling in SpooledTemporaryFile
3. **Content-Type detection**: Interfering with binary file processing
4. **Character encoding**: Binary data being processed as text somewhere

## Impact

This prevents FastAPI from being used for applications that need to handle Excel file uploads, which is a common business requirement.

## Request

Please investigate the binary file handling in FastAPI's upload pipeline. The fact that text-based files (CSV) work while binary files (XLSX) are corrupted suggests a fundamental issue with binary data preservation during the upload process.

## Test Case for Maintainers

1. Create a simple XLSX file with data
2. Upload it using the code above
3. Try to open the saved file with openpyxl
4. Observe the "Bad magic number" error

The same test with a CSV file works perfectly, confirming this is specific to binary file handling.

---

**Submitted by**: [Kevin Daniel/mFilterit]  
**Date**: [2025-08-08]
```

FastAPI is corrupting Excel (.xlsx) files during upload processing, while CSV files work perfectly. The corruption occurs before any user code processes the file, resulting in "Bad magic number for central directory" errors when attempting to open uploaded Excel files.

First, please check and fix the formatting of your message.

Second, could you create a code example without external dependencies?

The following code example receives file, saves it to tmp file and asserts that first bytes remain unchanged:

```py
from fastapi import FastAPI, File, UploadFile

app = FastAPI()


@app.post("/upload")
async def upload_file(file: UploadFile = File(...)):
    # Reset file pointer
    await file.seek(0)

    # Read file content
    content = await file.read()

    assert content.startswith(b"PK\x03\x04")

    # Save to temporary file
    temp_path = f"/tmp/{file.filename}"
    with open(temp_path, "wb") as f:
        f.write(content)

    with open(temp_path, "rb") as f:
        content_read = f.read()

    assert content_read.startswith(b"PK\x03\x04")

    return "ok"
```

This code works well on my machine. I see you are using Windows. Does it work on your machine?

title: Possible memory leak when using UploadFile
question_body: ### First Check - [X] I added a very descriptive title here. - [X] I used the GitHub search to find a similar question and didn't find it. - [X] I searched the FastAPI documentation, with the integrated search. - [X] I already searched in Google "How to X in FastAPI" and didn't find any information. - [X] I already read and followed all the tutorial in the docs and didn't find an answer. - [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [Pydantic](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic). - [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [Swagger UI](https://github.com/swagger-api/swagger-ui). - [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [ReDoc](https://github.com/Redocly/redoc). ### Commit to Help - [x] I commit to help with one of those options 👆 ### Example Code ```python @router.post("/projects", response_model=ProjectResponse, operation_id="projects_create") async def api_projects_create( request: fastapi.Request, name: Annotated[str, fastapi.Form()], software_name: Annotated[str, fastapi.Form()], skip_project_setup: Annotated[bool, fastapi.Form()] = False, project_setup_payload: Annotated[Json, fastapi.Form()] = {}, setup_files: Annotated[list[fastapi.UploadFile], fastapi.File()] = [], ): for input_file in setup_files: output_path = Path('sample_folder') / some_random_name() async with aiofiles.open(output_path, "wb") as out_file: while True: chunk = await input_file.read(CHUNK_FILE_SIZE) if not chunk: break await out_file.write(chunk) ``` ### Description I'm using UploadFile, for handling the upload of some files, in an endpoint like the one reported above. The endpoint is not exacly like that but the reported snippet it's pretty similar regarding what we do with the files. It's probably a specific use case because we have both Form and a list of UploadFile (that I'm not sure I've annotated correctly). The issue is that, even if I'm using UploadFile, the uploaded files seems to be loaded partially in RAM and never ever properly freed, even after minutes. > at 9:57 you can see the upload > here's the same with two uploads: one at 10:18, the second at 10:21. The memory delta is almost exacly the half of the size of the uploaded file We've done some investigations to search for a possible memory leak. First we created a FileUploadContext to ensure all files are closed in the endpoint: ```python class UploadFilesContext: def __init__(self, files: list[UploadFile]) -> None: self.files = files async def __aenter__(self): return self.files async def __aexit__(self, exc_type, exc_value, exc_tb): for file in self.files: try: await file.close() except BaseException: logging.exception("Unable to properly close file from UploadFilesContext") @router.post("/projects", response_model=ProjectResponse, operation_id="projects_create") async def api_projects_create( request: fastapi.Request, name: Annotated[str, fastapi.Form()], software_name: Annotated[str, fastapi.Form()], skip_project_setup: Annotated[bool, fastapi.Form()] = False, project_setup_payload: Annotated[Json, fastapi.Form()] = {}, setup_files: Annotated[list[fastapi.UploadFile], fastapi.File()] = [], ): async with UploadFilesContext(setup_files) as setup_files: ... # the rest like before ``` At this point we are pretty sure that all UploadFiles should be closed using the `close()` method. We have tried to check up memory references to sus classes: ```python async def test_debug(): data = {} for cls in ["UploadFile", "SpooledTemporaryFile", "BytesIO", "IO"]: data[cls] = objgraph.count(cls) objgraph.show_backrefs( objgraph.by_type("SpooledTemporaryFile")[:1], max_depth=5, filename=f"{uuid4()}.png" ) return data ``` And sometime we noticed that a SpooledTemporaryFile reference was hanging. Going further this should be the references tree: That might be related to this part of starlette code: https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/blob/main/starlette/datastructures.py#L478 and https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/blob/main/starlette/concurrency.py#L30 - Is it possible that FormData or UploadFile is memory leaking somewhere? - Is it correct to use list[UploadFile] like I did in the snippet? - Should I care to handle closing other resources from the endpoint? ### Operating System Linux ### Operating System Details Mainly happens inside a Docker context. ### FastAPI Version 0.121.2 ### Pydantic Version 2.12.4 ### Python Version 3.11.13 ### Additional Context _No response_
accepted_answer:
Hi @gbertoncelli-nw,

The `objgraph` trace pointing to `run_in_threadpool` is the key indicator here.

**The likely cause**
When you loop through the file with `await input_file.read(CHUNK_FILE_SIZE)`, you are dispatching a new task to the threadpool for *every single chunk*. For a large file, this creates thousands of short-lived thread tasks. This puts immense pressure on the `anyio` and `starlette` threadpool and the Python Garbage Collector, often leading to memory fragmentation or "soft leaks" where objects (like the captured `self.file` reference in the thread task) stay alive longer than expected.

**Solution**
Since `UploadFile` wraps a synchronous `SpooledTemporaryFile`, it is most efficient to perform the file copy completely synchronously within a *single* threadpool task, rather than switching back and forth between async and sync contexts for every chunk.

Try replacing your read/write loop with `shutil.copyfileobj` wrapped in `run_in_threadpool`. This moves the heavy lifting to a worker thread and keeps the main loop clean.

```python
import shutil
from starlette.concurrency import run_in_threadpool

# Define a sync helper function to do the copy
def save_file_sync(input_file_obj, output_path):
    with open(output_path, "wb") as buffer:
        shutil.copyfileobj(input_file_obj, buffer)

# Inside your endpoint
for input_file in setup_files:
    output_path = Path('sample_folder') / some_random_name()
    
    # Ensure the file cursor is at the start (just in case)
    await input_file.seek(0)
    
    # Run the blocking copy operation in a separate thread
    await run_in_threadpool(save_file_sync, input_file.file, output_path)
```

**your questions**

**Is `FormData` or `UploadFile` memory leaking?**
    Likely not the classes themselves, but the *usage pattern* involving thousands of `run_in_threadpool` calls creates references that are hard for the GC to clean up immediately. The `objgraph` references you see are likely the closures created for these thread tasks.

**Is it correct to use `list[UploadFile]`?**
    Yes, your annotation `Annotated[list[fastapi.UploadFile], fastapi.File()]` is correct. `python-multipart` handles this standardly.

*Should I care to handle closing other resources?**
    Your `UploadFilesContext` is excellent practice. However, if you switch to the `shutil` method above, you might find the manual closing is still necessary but the memory pressure will disappear because you aren't generating the massive object overhead during the read.

Yes indeed you can use this function to make sure you filter out logs from healthiness/readiness endpoints

```python
import logging

def register_log_filter() -> None:
    """
    Removes logs from healthiness/readiness endpoints so they don't spam
    and pollute application log flow
    """

    class EndpointFilter(logging.Filter):
        def filter(self, record: logging.LogRecord) -> bool:
            return (
                record.args  # type: ignore
                and len(record.args) >= 3
                and record.args[2] not in ["/_/health", "/_/ready"]  # type: ignore
            )

    logging.getLogger("uvicorn.access").addFilter(EndpointFilter())
```

title: FastAPI segfaults with Python 3.14.0 on MacOS
question_body:

- [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [ReDoc](https://github.com/Redocly/redoc).

### Commit to Help

- [X] I commit to help with one of those options 👆

### Example Code

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI

app = FastAPI()


@app.get("/")
def read_root():
    return {"Hello": "World"}


@app.get("/items/{item_id}")
def read_item(item_id: int, q: str | None = None):
    return {"item_id": item_id, "q": q}
```


### Description

* Create a new FastAPI environment e.g. with uv via the following
```
uv init .
echo "3.14.0" > .python-version
uv python install
uv add "fastapi[standard]"
```
* Run the example code via `uv run fastapi dev`.
FastAPI immediately segfaults:

```
❯ uv run fastapi dev --verbose
 ~/Programmieren/fastapi-segfault  main ?6                                                                  SEGV ✘  3.14.0    14:49:26
```

If I switch to Python 3.13, it works fine.

Demo repository can be found here: https://github.com/guerda/fastapi-segfaults

### Operating System

macOS

### Operating System Details

MacOS 15.7.7 (24G720)

### FastAPI Version

0.138.0 - this command fails too

### Pydantic Version

2.13.4

### Python Version

3.14.0

### Additional Context

_No response_
accepted_answer:
Look at the path in your  faulthandler output:

```
/Users/philip/.local/share/uv/python/cpython-3.14.0a6-macos-x86_64-none/lib/python3.14/...
```

That's not Python 3.14.0 final... it's **3.14.0 alpha 6** (`a6`). Even though your `.python-version` says `3.14.0` and `uv python install` ran without complaint, uv resolved to a stale alpha build it had cached from earlier in the 3.14 beta cycle, rather than downloading the actual final release. This is a known uv quirk. There are several open uv issues describing exactly this (astral-sh/uv#13361, #18414): a previously installed pre release CPython build gets reused/resolved instead of the version you asked for.

That fully explains the segfault. CPython alpha/beta builds are **not ABI-stable**... internal struct layouts can and do change between alpha6 and the final 3.14.0 release. `pydantic-core` (and friends like `uvloop`/`watchfiles`) ship compiled wheels built against the final 3.14 ABI. Load one of those into an alpha6 interpreter and you get a silent, traceback less SEGV - which is exactly what you saw, and exactly why it crashes deep inside `pydantic-core`'s class-creation code for `Secret` (that's the kind of code that touches CPython internals most directly).

**Fix:**

```bash
uv python list                      # confirm you have a stray cpython-3.14.0a6-... entry
uv python uninstall 3.14.0a6        # remove the alpha build
rm -rf .venv
uv python install 3.14.0            # explicit, full final version
uv run python -c "import sys; print(sys.version)"   # confirm it says 3.14.0, NOT 3.14.0a6
uv sync
uv run fastapi dev
```

If `uv python list` still offers the alpha as the resolved match for `3.14.0`, that's a uv bug worth reporting on astral-sh/uv directly... but it isn't a FastAPI or Pydantic bug.

    try:
        response = client.beta.messages.create(
            model="",
            messages=payload.get("messages"),
            mcp_servers=[...]
        result = response.json()

### Description

Function calling openai API.
Synchronization has been set up.

### Operating System

Windows

_No response_

### FastAPI Version

0.119.1

### Pydantic Version

2.12.3

3.11

### Additional Context

So I created a function to call openAI api as a synchronization request. The length of the message you send the request takes time to respond (for a few seconds). If I run this server as uvicorn and send the request to that function and send the request one more time before the response comes, can server use the method in the next request after the previous response ends?
accepted_answer:
As your function is `async` and there is no any `await` inside it, it will be executed in one go without interruption.
So, your worker will only be able to handle 1 request at a time.

If you need to use blocking code in your endpoint functions (like you do in this code example), either convert this endpoint to sync (remove `async` from function signature) or use `run_in_threadpool` to run blocking code inside `async` function.

One more alternative (in your case better use on of the approaches above) is to make `client.beta.messages.create` async and add some `await asyncio.sleep(0)` inside it to let event loop execute other tasks.
